findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Uncaptured returned mutable mapping loses handed spend on restore
findings.smallest_reproduction: S2/native.py depths145/146 at recursion limit150: dispatch once, return spent owner mapping, capture/recovery RecursionError, restore earlier ledger in mapping, redispatch original admitted action.
findings.actual_result: Raw pending mapping revision2 changes to1; refusal false; executor calls2; sealed null.
findings.expected_result: Handed spend retained sufficiently to refuse original action after restore, calls1.
findings.proposed_correction: Select a narrow owner publication/lifetime guarantee preserving the content until stable capture and appropriate acknowledgement. Cover restore and interruption. Do not silently weaken all-returned-handings scope.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Incomplete JSON normalization falsely retires honest numeric-key histories
findings.smallest_reproduction: S2/test_independent.py::test_normalization: new ledger detail or experiment metadata with nested {2:a,10:b}; interrupted handed retention; exact owner JSON restored checkpoint; read twice.
findings.actual_result: Both numeric-key baseline cases permanently refuse with rewrote its history; fresh reader accepts same restored owner. Equivalent string-key cases recover.
findings.expected_result: Owner-equivalent restored history recovers without divergence.
findings.proposed_correction: Reconcile retained entries through complete matching owner JSON/write/read normalization before hashing, preserving separate ledger and experiment serialization semantics and existing incompatibility refusal. Straightforward local direction, no lifetime decision needed.
findings.sensitivity: Scratch-only monkeypatch wraps _history: JSON dumps(sort_keys=True,default=str), JSON loads, matching BudgetCharge/ScientificEvaluation.from_dict, then original _history. Four cases (numeric/string x ledger/experiment) recover. This normalizes BOTH current and retained histories and is only a bounded sensitivity experiment; not production fix implementation, no proof of complete owner serialization equivalence or compatibility. Production should match ledger and scientific experiment serialization paths exactly.

architecture_decision_analysis.conclusion: Explicit lifetime/handoff decision needed for complete guarantee under admitted repeated pre-capture interruption plus mutable replacement; local remedies remain possible for narrower reachable checkpoints.
architecture_decision_analysis.reason: After both native captures abort before retaining any entry, the only saved mapping aliases mutable owner storage. Once overwritten, reader-accessible state no longer contains the spend. Later re-read cannot distinguish lost-spend case from honest unchanged content in general. Refusing indefinitely/permanent sealing solely for interruption violates honest-recovery obligation; accepting reconstructed old content violates preservation.
architecture_decision_analysis.qualification: This is conditional information-loss reasoning, not a formal impossibility theorem for every reader implementation. Fresh-stack retry can fix this native recursion trigger. Incremental retention can fix a second-map interruption after first-map data was copied. More finite retries move the earliest failure window. A retention/immutable return/acknowledgement protocol can be narrow and use existing owners; no second budget authority is required. D2/F2 is separable local normalization work. No protocol selected or implemented.
